module.title: Auditing AI-Written Code
module.subtitle: Spotting mutable default traps, silent assumptions, and weak assertions
lesson_points: AI-generated code often looks clean on the happy path while hiding classic Python traps at boundaries.
Trap #1 — Mutable default args: 'def add_tag(tag, tags=[]):' shares ONE list across every call instead of creating a new list!
Trap #2 — Weak tests: Always inspect whether assertions test empty lists, duplicates, negative numbers, and repeated calls.
module.example_code:
def add_tag_safe(tag, tags=None):
    if tags is None:
        tags = []
    tags.append(tag)
    return tags

a = add_tag_safe("python")
b = add_tag_safe("visual")
assert a == ["python"]
assert b == ["visual"]
print("Independent lists:", a, b)

quizzes.title: The Mutable Default Bug
quizzes.prompt: An AI wrote 'items=[]' as a default parameter. What does the second call print?
quizzes.code:
def append_log(msg, items=[]):
    items.append(msg)
    return items

first = append_log("boot")
second = append_log("ready")
print(second)
quizzes.explanation: Default list [] is created ONCE when 'def' runs, so both calls share and mutate the same list!

quizzes.title: Spot the Off-by-One Access Bug
quizzes.prompt: Click the line in this AI-written helper that skips checking the last item or crashes on empty input.
quizzes.explanation: Python slice end index is exclusive, so stopping at len(items) - 1 drops the last item (returns [20] instead of [20, 30]). Use items[-2:]!

quizzes.title: Reviewing a Suspiciously Green Test
quizzes.prompt: If an AI agent submits a function plus 'assert calc([1, 2]) == 3', what should you ask before trusting it?
quizzes.sample_explanation: Check what happens on edge cases not tested—such as empty lists [], None, negative numbers, or non-number inputs.
quizzes.explanation: Single happy-path assertions prove almost nothing about boundary safety; auditing missing test cases is the fastest way to catch silent flaws.
